results.trace: Ran `pnpm vitest run --config vitest.config.ts tests/verify/R2-1.test.ts`. I mocked createRaceScene so it advances fake timers by 300 ms, which stands in for a slow scene build. Then I clicked RACE on the menu (mode becomes 'race') and advanced 250 ms. Result: `expected null not to be null`, so [data-screen-change="chequer"] was already gone. game.ts:110-113 arms the 330 ms timer in playScreenChange (screen-change.ts:53) before the synchronous startRace. The CSS sweep can only start painting after startRace returns.
results.reason: The removal timer starts before the blocking race start, so slow start work shortens the visible chequer sweep or removes it entirely. Calling playScreenChange after startRace fixes it, and AC8 still holds.

results.trace: Ran the test. It renders createStartScreen with three cards, then dispatches ArrowLeft with altKey, ctrlKey or metaKey on the first card. The first case fails with `expected true to be false` on e.defaultPrevented. start-screen.ts:56-62 has no modifier guard, while keyboard.ts:41 returns early on ctrl, meta or alt.
results.reason: Arrow keys with Alt, Ctrl or Meta are swallowed (preventDefault) and change the track, which blocks browser shortcuts such as Alt+Left for Back. The game's own keyboard input deliberately leaves these alone.

results.trace: Ran the test. It renders the screen-change--stripes stage with localStorage cleared, then again with racer.bestLap.<first track>=40370. The text differs: Received 'Bramble BendsBEST 0:40.37' where 'BEST –:––.––' was expected. screen-change.stage.ts:10 passes no bestLaps, so start-screen.ts falls back to localBestLaps.
results.reason: stage.ts says a stage must be deterministic, but this stage's output depends on real browser storage. start.stage.ts avoids that by passing memoryBestLaps.

results.trace: The new rule at src/ui/title.css:93-101, `.ui-start__label { margin:0; font-family:var(--type-title-font); font-size:var(--type-title-size); font-weight:var(--type-title-weight); font-style:var(--type-title-style); line-height:1; text-transform:uppercase; }`, has exactly the same declarations as the existing `.ui-pause__title` at src/ui/screens.css:82-90. start-screen.ts already imports screens.css (line 5), so the existing rule could cover the new heading as well.
results.reason: The new CSS block copies an existing rule line for line, and that rule does the same job (title type style). A shared selector would remove the copy.

results.trace: Compared start.stage.ts:12 with game.ts:148. Both are new in this diff, so there is no existing helper being re-implemented. The stage fixtures already hard-code the stride in the same way (stage.ts:72 `outline: centre.filter((_, i) => i % 8 === 0)`, pre-existing).
results.reason: This is a one-line fixture expression, not a copy of an existing helper. Stages build their own fixed data by convention, and stage.ts already hard-codes the stride 8. Dropped as a style preference.

results.trace: UI_RULES.md:109 (§10) requires every new element to define a pressed state, and :105 says 'Pressed = sink onto a 1px shadow'. In src/ui/title.css the track card has only default, :focus-visible and :hover/:focus-visible lift rules (lines 112-138). There is no `.ui-track-card:active` anywhere in src/ui. The :hover lift (line 136) is also outside `@media (hover: hover)`, unlike `.ui-button` (components.css:143-144), so on touch screens the lift sticks after a tap.
results.reason: The new track card element has no pressed state, which UI_RULES §10 requires, and its hover lift is not limited to hover-capable devices the way the existing button component is.

results.trace: UI_RULES.md:57 (§5): 'Desktop: same layout at ×1.45, 32px margins, 4px outlines.' Screenshot 1440x900/stage/start--menu.png shows the new S6 screen at mobile sizes: the heading is about 56px (mobile display size), the cards are about 144px wide in a 960px panel, the RACE button is mobile size and the brand margin is 48px. src/ui/title.css has no desktop rules and createStartScreen never calls watchDesktop (src/ui/layout.ts:20), while the HUD does (hud.ts:95, hud.css .is-desktop rules).
results.reason: The newly built S6 screen ignores the explicit desktop scaling rule in UI_RULES §5. The 1440×900 screenshot shows it at phone sizes with most of the panel empty.
